steps.label: Discover
steps.question: What is here, and where?
steps.definition: How an agent learns that a resource, tool or agent exists at an origin, and where to find its description.

steps.label: Identify
steps.question: Who is this agent? Who is this site?
steps.definition: How an agent proves who it is to a site, and how a site or another agent proves who it is back.

steps.label: Permit
steps.question: What may the agent do here?
steps.definition: How a site states what agents may read, train on, or do, and how agents obtain authorisation to act.

steps.label: Read
steps.question: Give me the content
steps.definition: Representations of a site's content made for machine readers rather than browsers.

steps.label: Act
steps.question: Do something for me
steps.definition: How an agent invokes a capability a site or tool exposes.

steps.label: Coordinate
steps.question: Talk to another agent
steps.definition: How agents delegate to, negotiate with, and message other agents.

steps.label: Pay
steps.question: Settle the bill
steps.definition: How an agent pays for a resource, authorises a payment on a person's behalf, or completes a purchase.

steps.label: Present
steps.question: Show a human the result
steps.definition: How an agent renders output or a live interaction to a person.

steps.label: Account
steps.question: Prove what happened; be judged
steps.definition: How actions are recorded, verified after the fact, attributed and measured.

parties.label: agent ↔ site
parties.definition: An agent interacting with a website or API origin.

parties.label: agent ↔ human
parties.definition: An agent presenting to, or taking instruction from, a person.

parties.label: agent ↔ payment network
parties.definition: An agent and a payment rail, wallet, or card network.

parties.label: agent ↔ registry
parties.definition: An agent and a third-party index or registry.

form.label: well-known file
form.definition: A fixed-path file under /.well-known/ or the site root.

form.label: endpoint
form.definition: An HTTP or RPC endpoint with a defined message format.

form.label: DNS record
form.definition: A record type or name convention in DNS.

form.label: on-chain registry
form.definition: A smart contract acting as a registry.

form.label: document format
form.definition: A file format or document convention.

form.label: browser API
form.definition: A JavaScript API available to pages in a browser.

track.label: IETF
track.definition: Internet Engineering Task Force draft or RFC.

track.label: W3C
track.definition: W3C working or community group output.

track.label: Linux Foundation
track.definition: A Linux Foundation project or sub-foundation.

track.label: industry body
track.definition: A trade association such as IAB Tech Lab.

track.label: vendor consortium
track.definition: Several vendors publishing jointly without a standards body.

track.label: community
track.definition: Open community project with no formal governance.

track.label: academic
track.definition: Research output without a standards process.

scope.label: general
scope.definition: Applies to any site or agent.

scope.label: commerce
scope.definition: Buying and selling goods or services.

phase.label: draft
phase.definition: Specification text exists and is changing.

phase.label: working group
phase.definition: Adopted by a standards working group.

phase.label: review
phase.definition: In formal review or last call.

phase.label: living
phase.definition: Continuously updated with no versioned finals.

phase.label: deprecated
phase.definition: Superseded or discouraged by its issuer.

implementation.label: developer trial
implementation.definition: Behind a flag or origin trial.

implementation.label: multi-implementation
implementation.definition: Independent production implementations from more than one party.

adoption.label: claimed
adoption.definition: A party asserts adoption; the claimant is named.

adoption.label: observed
adoption.definition: We or a third party have seen instances but not counted systematically.

adoption.label: measured
adoption.definition: Counted by a documented probe run.

evidence.label: verified
evidence.definition: Primary source, or two independent secondary sources, checked by us.

use_cases.label: Let agents discover my API or service
use_cases.definition: Publish where an agent can find what an origin offers.

use_cases.label: Expose tools to agents
use_cases.definition: Let a model call functions or actions you host.

use_cases.label: Let agents act on my website
use_cases.definition: Forms, bookings and tasks performed by agents in a browser or via a page-level API.

use_cases.label: Serve readable content to agents
use_cases.definition: Give agents a machine-friendly version of pages and documents.

use_cases.label: Prove an agent's identity
use_cases.definition: Let a server verify which agent, operator or workload is calling.

use_cases.label: Delegate a user's authority to an agent
use_cases.definition: Scoped, revocable permission for an agent to act for a person.

use_cases.label: Control AI crawling and training use
use_cases.definition: State what automated systems may do with your content.

use_cases.label: Accept payments from agents
use_cases.definition: Charge an agent per request or per purchase.

use_cases.label: Let agents buy on behalf of a person
use_cases.definition: Mandates, carts and checkout flows for agent purchases.

use_cases.label: Let agents talk to other agents
use_cases.definition: Discover, message and delegate between independent agents.

use_cases.label: Name and resolve agents
use_cases.definition: Stable names or records that resolve to an agent's endpoint.

use_cases.label: Render agent output as a user interface
use_cases.definition: Structured UI that a client renders from an agent.

use_cases.label: Audit what an agent did
use_cases.definition: Tamper-evident records of actions and the authority behind them.

use_cases.label: Attribute and measure agent traffic
use_cases.definition: Know which agents visited and what they did.

use_cases.label: Describe an agent's capabilities
use_cases.definition: Cards, manifests and schemas that say what an agent can do.

audience.label: Site or API owner
audience.definition: Runs a website, API or shop that agents will use.

audience.label: Agent builder
audience.definition: Builds agents or the frameworks they run on.

audience.label: Platform or infrastructure
audience.definition: CDNs, identity providers, payment networks, registries.

audience.label: Standards and policy
audience.definition: People shaping or tracking the specifications themselves.
